doc.title: Laurena Diggs and Carrie Boote Interview, 1959-05-25

chapter: Punch Miller and musicians she knew
title: Punch Miller as a lodger, his fans, and Joe Glaser
summary: Punch roomed with her; women called for him; he passed up manager Joe Glaser.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: You said your phone would ring one.

No, I was talking about the different people when they found where Punch was living at. They would ring, he, he roomed with me, you know. And I said different women, white and colored would call it. I had to put a very rich woman out of my home. He can tell you about his, uh, singing. She came there with her chauffeur and all. And Punch can tell you I had to ask her out. And she wanted Punch to sing, and just, because at that time I wasn't broad enough to understand, but she just wanted to hear him sing. She said no harm, she said. That was her pleasure, and her husband had her chauffeur to take her anywhere she wanted to go, and she paid for whatever she wanted. But I didn't care to be bothered, and I wouldn't allow her to come in. Punch can tell you. And they, and she, he, they would call night and day for Punch. Punch had a very good voice before he, he made records too, you know. And he did pretty good, but it just seemed like some people gets to the top, they have more business abilities, and some don't. And then when you have a good manager, Joe Glazer wanted Punch once, but, uh, you know, Punch, Joe, they want so much, and this thing and the other. And he had nobody told him just how to go about, and he wouldn't go on, but if he had went with Joe Glazer, maybe he would have been, you know, popular today. But he thought it was bad not to.
